title: Login screen
description: The sign-in screen as the reference composition for a whole screen built from the contract: a stage (chosen 2026-09-25 at /lab/login-2 over a photo panel beside the form, a framed sheet and a dark pane), in parts the route arranges on a ground it composes itself: no stage component (retired 2026-10-01, composition over coupling), the route lays a full-bleed region with the ImageOverlay at low clarity and the BackgroundNoise as its first children and the parts after them. LoginBar holds LoginBrand (the wordmark) and LoginNav (the visitor's actions); LoginCard is the glass Card centred in the middle row, whose header the route fills from Card's own parts (a title, a lede); LoginForm is the two ways in on one panel (since 2026-10-01, after the PubDash sign-in): the hero Single sign-on button, an "or" rule, the two required Inputs, a slotted help link, the primary Sign in and a slotted footnote; LoginFooter is one line at the foot. One composition for phone and desktop, tightened below 40rem of the full-bleed region.

anatomy.description: Composed by the route, not a part: a section with the global full-bleed class (min-height 100svh, the page gutters, an inline-size container named full-bleed) holding ImageOverlay at low clarity and BackgroundNoise as its first children, then the login parts; the route's own module arranges the rows. There is no LoginStage (retired 2026-10-01): a wrapper that owned the ground, the layers, the rows and the container coupled four unrelated decisions into one login-only element (component-architecture §4.7.1).
A header with data-slot="login-bar": a flex row, space-between, for LoginBrand on the left and LoginNav on the right.

A span with data-slot="login-brand" that sizes the svg inside it (7.5rem wide, 5.5rem below 40rem) and colours it needle-900 through currentColor. The route imports the wordmark asset and drops it in.

A nav with data-slot="login-nav": a 0.5rem row for the visitor's actions, Buttons asChild around router Links (a secondary link and the one primary of the bar; secondary rather than discrete because the stage is a photograph, where a discrete button's lift has nothing to cast on).

The house Card in glass (data-slot="card", data-material="glass"; chosen 2026-09-28 once the stage took the photograph), centred in the middle row: the width up to 26rem, 1.75rem 2rem padding (1.5rem 1.25rem below 40rem), the md radius, the bark-200 hairline at 60%. Its module gives the card's header 1.25rem below.
Composed by the route from Card's parts: CardTitle at level 1 (the page's main content) over a one-line CardDescription lede.

react-aria Form with data-slot="login-form", a 1rem column centred at 22rem, nothing but markup and two controlled strings: no effect, no ref, no measurement. The Sign in button is disabled until both fields hold a value (2026-10-01), so an empty submit cannot happen; native validation still checks the email's shape on submit and FieldError shows the message; onSubmit hands the credentials to the caller. With onSingleSignOn, the hero Single sign-on button and the divider come first; without it the email takes focus on load.

A p with data-slot="login-divider", only with onSingleSignOn: the word "or" as a caps eyebrow (text-xs, 600, 0.07em, bark-500) between two 1px bark-300 hairlines, read by assistive tech as the word it is.
Under the Sign in button, only with a footnote: the footnote (a p at text-sm, bark-900, whose links are needle-800 and answer in bloom on hover).
A p with data-slot="login-footer": one centred line at text-sm, bloom-800, in the stage's last row (the copyright, a privacy link, the demo's disclaimer).

usage: A reference composition, not a reusable primitive: copy the structure (a stage in three rows, a glass Card in the middle, the header from Card's parts, the form from Field-composed controls) rather than the components.

The route arranges: <section className={cn(styles.stage, "full-bleed")}><ImageOverlay clarity="low" /><BackgroundNoise /><LoginBar><LoginBrand>…</LoginBrand><LoginNav>…</LoginNav></LoginBar><LoginCard><CardHeader>…</CardHeader><LoginForm … /></LoginCard><LoginFooter>…</LoginFooter></section>. The title, the lede, the bar's actions, the help link, the footnote and the footer are the route's words and links; the route's module arranges the rows and never touches the parts.

Controlled: onSignIn({ email, password }) is all the form reports and the component never navigates; the route decides where a sign-in lands. Ask for nothing user-scoped before sign-in (workspaces, names, plans): the authenticated shell resolves those once it knows who signed in.

Pass onSingleSignOn (no arguments) to render the hero Single sign-on button and the "or" rule above the fields; leave it out and the form is the credentials alone, with the email focused on load. Pass helpAction and footnote as nodes built from Button asChild and router Links so the router stays in the route.
Add a third way in as another button above the divider, never as a panel: the form stayed one panel on purpose (2026-10-01), so every way in is on screen at once and the component needs no effect.

The card is glass because the stage carries a photograph: the route lays the ImageOverlay at low clarity and the BackgroundNoise under everything (2026-09-28; by the route since 2026-10-01), and a card on a photograph is glass, never flat (Card's usage). Nothing in the composition depends on the photograph loading: the ground under it is the overlay's own gradient.

Sign in stays disabled until both fields hold a value; beyond that, validation is react-aria's native behaviour: do not add noValidate or an attempted-submit flag. Messages come through errorMessage on each Input.
The alternatives this was chosen from (a photo panel beside the form, a framed sheet, the dark pane) stay at /lab/login-2 as the archive; the first round at /lab/login.

Few icons: the SSO button is words alone and the switches point with a typographic arrow in the label, not a chevron icon (component-architecture §3.10). Add an icon here only for a meaning the words do not carry.

Compose, do not couple: there is no stage component, and a copy of this screen MUST NOT add one. The ground, the layers, the rows and the container each stand alone in the route, so any one can change without a prop or a second wrapper (component-architecture §4.7.1).
